commit_message:
[maglev] Introduce MapInference

This CL introduces `MapInference`, similar to TurboFan, to manage map
knowledge in Maglev.  Instead of clearing possible maps on side effects,
we now mark them as stale. This allows us to either ignore them or
re-verify them using `CheckMaps`.

All previous users of NodeInfo::possible_maps were updated to use the
MapInference interface; in addition to fetching the set of possible
maps, they are now required to call InsertMapChecks once the decision
has been made to use possible_maps.

InsertMapChecks only emits map checks when needed, ie when at least one
stale unstable map exists. Unreliable maps are "stale" when a side
effect may have occurred after we've last recorded them.

The --maglev-use-unreliable-maps flag, on by default, currently controls
whether Maglev uses stale unreliable maps by default, ie when no
explicit variant is passed to MapInference methods. Note that there is
no guarantee that *not* enabling this flag is identical to previous
behavior, since map tracking changed underneath (it should be similar
though). This flag is likely to be removed soon.

This CL also introduces KNA tracing: --trace-maglev-kna.

fix_commit_message:
[maglev] Don't swallow aborts in TryInferApiHolderValue

InsertMapChecks can abort (and null current_block_), but we'd
return the default "not found" sentinel, causing the caller in
TryBuildCallKnownApiFunction to fall through and emit a
CallBuiltin into a dead block. AttachExceptionHandlerInfo then
dereferences current_block_ and crashes.

Return std::optional instead; nullopt means the caller must
propagate DoneWithAbort.

Fixed: 503634281
Change-Id: Ic066c968f308c2a05c445150ac97a8ef2a9df304
Reviewed-on: https://chromium-review.googlesource.com/c/v8/v8/+/7789170

Reviewed-by: Darius Mercadier <dmercadier@chromium.org>

agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 604e1bec5911 on top of intro 8a41470735aa via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (NullPointerDereference): In V8's Maglev compiler, MaglevGraphBuilder::TryInferApiHolderValue() attempts to statically infer the 'holder' object for an API function call based on known receiver map information. As part of this, it calls MapInference::InsertMapChecks(), which can internally decide that graph building must abort (nulling out the builder's current basic block, e.g. current_block_) if it cannot safely insert the required map-check nodes. However, TryInferApiHolderValue() only had a single return type (compiler::HolderLookupResult) and mapped both the abort case and the legitimate 'holder could not be inferred' case to the same 'not_found' sentinel value. Its caller, TryBuildCallKnownApiFunction(), used this sentinel to decide to fall through and build a generic CallBuiltin node, unaware that graph building had actually aborted. This caused further IR nodes (including exception handler attachment via AttachExceptionHandlerInfo) to be emitted against an invalid/null current_block_, leading to a null-pointer dereference and crash. Root cause: Conflating two semantically distinct outcomes ('holder not found' vs 'graph building aborted') into a single sentinel return value, so the caller cannot detect that the compiler has entered a dead/aborted state and must stop emitting nodes.
